Revenue / Subscription economics

Gross-profit CAC payback period

The modeled number of months required for a new customer's monthly gross profit to recover fully loaded acquisition cost. Gross profit uses revenue minus the agreed cost of serving that customer, rather than revenue alone.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The modeled number of months required for a new customer's monthly gross profit to recover fully loaded acquisition cost. Gross profit uses revenue minus the agreed cost of serving that customer, rather than revenue alone.

months

How we use it

Useful for planning the cash needed to fund growth. We can show cohort payback curves when customer revenue and margin vary over time.

Transparent calculationFully loaded CAC ÷ (monthly average revenue per new customer × gross-margin fraction)
fully loaded cac1,250
monthly revenue per new customer200
gross margin percent75

1,250 ÷ (200 × 0.75) = approximately 8.33 months, assuming constant monthly gross profit.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • New-customer acquisition cohort
  • Plan and gross margin
  • Channel and segment

Questions we investigate

  • Are CAC and customer gross profit scoped consistently?
  • Does churn delay actual recovery?
  • Do discounts or onboarding costs alter the scenario?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Review observed cohort cash and gross profit.
  • Reconcile fully loaded CAC and margin inputs.
  • Compare assumptions with retention and billing patterns.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Finance and revenue operations leads
Monthly after cost and recurring-value reconciliation.

Required data

  • Fully loaded cohort CAC
  • Monthly revenue per new customer and gross margin
  • Retention, billing, and allocation assumptions

Read the measure with context

Zero or negative monthly gross profit gives no finite positive recovery period. The simple formula ignores churn, payment delays, expansion, and time value of money. Modeled payback is not evidence that every acquired customer will repay CAC before leaving.
